title: Set up a client's portal and invite them
summary: Choose what a client sees in their portal, preview it, send the invite, and manage their sign-in once they join.

chapters.label: The client portal gives Mark and Laura their own secure sign-in.
Open Portal at the top of their plan to set it up.
Features picks which sections appear in their portal.
Turn off Calculators if they won't use it. It saves right away.
Editing is on by default, so they can update their own details.
Switch it off and they can view their portal but change nothing.
Preview Client Portal shows exactly what they'll see.
Calculators is gone from their menu.
With editing on, changes you make in the preview are saved.
Intake form sends a data-collection form, blank or pre-filled.
Access sends the invite. Mark's email comes from his CRM contact.
Send invite emails Mark a link to create his sign-in.
It reads Invited until he signs up. You can resend or revoke it.
Once Mark signs up, it turns Active and shows his last sign-in.
Send sign-in link emails him a one-time link if he's locked out.
Sign out everywhere ends his sessions on every device.
Remove portal access ends his access but keeps his login.
Delete login erases his login at every firm. It can't be undone.
Activity lists each change Mark makes in his portal.

steps: **Open the Portal tab.** From a client, choose **Portal** at the top of their plan.

**Choose their sections.** Under **Features**, switch off any section they won't use: **Investments**, **Budget**, **Documents** or **Calculators**. Each change saves right away. **Dashboard**, **Organizer** and **Settings** are always included.
**Decide whether they can edit.** **Editing** is on by default, so they can update their details and link accounts. Switch it off for a view-only portal.
**Preview it.** **Preview Client Portal** opens their portal in a new tab, exactly as they'll see it.

**Send the invite.** Under **Access**, check the **Client email** (it comes from their CRM contact) and select **Send invite**. The card reads **Invited** until they sign up. From there you can **Resend invite** or **Revoke invite**.

**Manage their sign-in.** Once they sign up, the card turns **Active** and shows their last sign-in. **Send sign-in link** emails a one-time link, **Sign out everywhere** ends their sessions, and **Remove portal access** ends access to this household but keeps their login. **Delete login** erases the login at every firm and can't be undone.
**Watch for changes.** **Activity** lists each change the client makes in their portal.
goodToKnow: With editing on, anything you change in the preview saves to the client's account.
If the email already has a Foundry account, Foundry sends an access request instead of an invite, and the client approves it from their own sign-in.
**Intake form** sends a data-collection form, blank or pre-filled from the plan. A blank form works even without portal access.
